messages:
alex: Heads-up — CI microbench flagged PR #19601 with a regression on the KV hotpath. Latency up ~12% on small-seq workloads. https://ci.internal/runs/98765 :eyes:
ci-bot: [alert] perf-threshold-diff: pr=19601 base=main metric=kv_hotpath_p50 diff=+12.3% (threshold=+5%)
perf-bot: Attached artifacts: /artifacts/pr-19601/bench-output.tar.gz and flamegraph.svg
maria: Ugh. Which changes in that PR? I remember it touched kernel-autoselect + a new kv-eviction heuristic. Could be interaction.
alex: Right — PR modifies kernel selector heuristics (cost-model tweak) and adds a small-kv-evict path to free slots earlier. Locally I repro the microbench on ./tools/microbench --suite=kv-hotpath --seq=32 --iters=100
jin: Sharing quick profiler snapshot from the CI node (top of stack):
```
# perf top (diff vs baseline)
+ kernel_select::score_evaluation  28%  (<baseline 6%)
+ kv_cache::evict_if_needed        12%  (baseline 3%)
+ runtime::dispatch_loop           10%  (baseline 9%)
```
jin: Also the KV hit rate from the CI run dropped 0.45 -> 0.22 for that trace. That explains token tail latency widening.
sam: If kernel_select is spending that much more time, maybe the new scoring loop iterates over candidate kernels more aggressively for short sequences. Could be O(n^2) in pathological cases.

maria: Can someone run a bisect? Quick check: revert the kernel selector tweak first, then kv-eviction. Which commit ranges are safe?
alex: I'll kick off a narrow bisect: revert only the kernel-autoselect change in a branch and run microbench. Submitted job: https://ci.internal/job/bench/98801

ci-bot: bench 98801 queued -> running on runner-14 (gpu-rt)

ops-bot: deploy notice: PR 19601 was merged 18m ago, routing policy rolled out to canary (5% traffic). No customer incidents yet.
dave: If canary shows increased p95 we should revert. Can we triage faster?

alex: Bisect result: reverting kernel-autoselect tweak drops p50 back to baseline, kv-hit still slightly low. Numbers: baseline p50=12ms, pr-19601 p50=13.4ms (+11.7%), revert-kernel p50=12.1ms (+0.8%).
maria: So kernel selector is the main culprit. The kv-evict change only amplifies misses but isn't primary.

jin: Quick diff of the change: the new score loop adds an extra pass to compare memory footprint for each candidate when seq_len<=64. That loop accidentally evaluates a larger set due to a boundary bug. Patch suggestion: short-circuit when candidates>8.
sam: Can you paste the offending snippet?
jin: ```cpp
for (auto &c : candidates) {
  evaluate_score(c);
  if (seq_len <= 64) {
    for (auto &d : candidates) { // <- this inner loop was meant to iterate over top_k, but bug uses full candidates list
      compare_memory(c,d);
    }
  }
}
```

maria: Ok that explains O(n^2) blowup on wide candidate pools. Impact is worse for small sequences we optimize for.
dave: Request: revert kernel change in prod canary and halt rollout until fix is merged. Ops, can you do an emergency rollback?

ops-bot: Initiating canary rollback for config/runtime-selector at 2026-03-20T15:12Z. Canary -> baseline.

ci-bot: CI run 98801 finished: bench delta now within threshold after revert (diff +0.9%). Full logs: https://ci.internal/job/bench/98801/logs

alex: I'll open PR to revert the kernel-autoselect commit (PR 19612) and include the fix branch with the short-circuit.
maria: After revert lands and CI is green we can re-run longer stress tests and a small canary with 1% traffic. Also add a microbench unit test for candidates>8 to prevent regressions.
sam: Filing a follow-up perf-test: add a golden-case that asserts kernel selector iteration count < 40 for seq<=64.

jin: Pushed fix branch and reverted in prod canary. Verified local microbench shows avg select time down 4x.

dave: Nice work. Follow-up action items?
maria: 1) PR 19612 revert (merged) 2) PR 19613 fix + unit tests 3) Add telemetry: count candidate_evaluations per request and alert if > 50 4) Postmortem note in eng-runtime.
alex: I'll create the postmortem draft and link bench artifacts.

perf-bot: Regression resolved in canary. Marking thread resolved after stability window (1h) if no further deltas. :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks team. Leaving logs and artifact links in the ticket.
